correctness.rationale: PASS: For every infinite well-orderable κ, color a pair α<β by whether g(α)≤g(β) or g(α)>g(β). The ZF Erdős–Dushnik–Miller partition theorem (or Shen Corollary 3.3) yields a size-κ nondecreasing homogeneous set: an ω-sized strictly decreasing set of ordinals is impossible. Iteration through any fixed finite list of g_i keeps the full cardinality and previously established monotonicity. For the ZFC obstruction, inject e:ω1→2^ω, allowed by ω1≤2^{aleph0}; define f_{2n}=1-e_n and f_{2n+1}=e_n. For distinct codes one of these two coordinates decreases along either order, so any common nondecreasing subset has at most one element. CH is unnecessary. No finite experiment needed; the two cases and cardinal assumptions are an exhaustive proof. The primary Shen paper full text was not retrieved; its one-map consequence also follows directly from the standard EDM theorem.

value.rationale: PASS, narrowly: This is a natural exact quantifier boundary for attempting to extend a newly published monotone-subset theorem from finitely to countably many requirements: every finite conjunction preserves an uncountable common subset, but countably many Boolean requirements can prevent even a two-point one. The proof is elementary and reuses a standard antichain mechanism; its worth is the sharp, explicitly motivated failure of countable iteration, not a new result about Cantor antichains or general infinite-dimensional posets. The scope is intentionally modest and the risk of folklore coverage is significant.
